source.title: Post-Training Science for Supervised Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Charles O'Neill; M. Jayasekara; Harry B. Partridge

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures scaling in supervised fine-tuning and refines the scope of a single scaling law: its size fits are saturating and recipe-dependent, its data-volume test is local rather than a full joint law, and repeated passes show overfitting rather than continued loss decay. It does not directly test the original pretraining scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own SFT size fits, fresh-data experiments, epoch results, and loss-to-downstream comparisons. It also discusses pretraining scaling laws in the introduction and cites other studies; those cited results are not recorded as rows. The study does not sweep training compute or find a compute-optimal parameter/token split.
record.test_reason: The study fits its own saturating power laws of SFT validation loss against model size, measures loss against fresh-example count and epochs, and correlates loss with judged downstream quality. That is a new setting (supervised fine-tuning) with results bearing on V5, V6 and V7. It does not test pretraining loss laws, extrapolation of pretraining fits, compute-optimal allocation, or shape at fixed parameter count.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. At the defaults, SFT loss falls as a saturating power law in size, steeper for FullFT, with LoRA's gap narrowing with scale. MoEs fit the trend at the geometric mean of active and total parameters. Fresh-example gains are dataset-specific but size-independent. Past about two epochs loss overfits while judged quality does not improve and IFEval erodes. Loss ranks quality within a recipe but not across families. The authors treat directions as robust and magnitudes as uncertain, given six sizes and four datasets.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies supervised fine-tuning with customer datasets and validation NLL, rather than fitting the original pretraining loss laws or compute-optimal pretraining allocations. Its size fits use six Qwen3 sizes at recommended SFT defaults; its data study is a local example-count interaction test.
record.method_sensitivity: The size exponents vary by dataset and tuner; the FullFT support exponent changes under oracle-learning-rate refitting. Dataset changes the gain from additional examples. Loss-to-evaluation relationships vary by model family, tuner, and dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: At matched loss within a recipe, Fisher-trace flatness ranks judged quality worse than loss and with the wrong sign for Llama FullFT. Across optimisers it tracks IFEval retention (ρs −0.71).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss-landscape flatness of SFT minima predicts retained general capability but not in-domain quality beyond loss.

fits_no_version.finding: The optimal LoRA learning rate is flat at 1e-3 across 0.6–32B (exponent p+q ≈0), about 33× the FullFT optimum.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The optimal SFT learning rate is size-invariant for LoRA.

fits_no_version.finding: Token load explains most of the final SFT NLL (R²≈0.6) and sets the fitted floor L∞.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dataset token composition sets the SFT loss floor.

record.problems: The authors note that the size fits use only six points per Qwen3 dataset/tuner, have wide exponent intervals, and may miss regime breaks. The data-volume test is local and examples remain confounded with tokens within a dataset. There are only four customer datasets, and their training data is optimized to pass the same customer evaluation used as the downstream judge.
record.rows_left_out: No additional relevant numeric scaling or downstream-predictability results were omitted. The reported MoE placement comparisons are not separately tabulated by model and tuner in the text as assignable values, so they are not given separate rows.

untested.parts: All of it: no held-out pretraining loss and no parameter, token or compute scaling in pretraining.
All of it for pretraining. Scoring Llama against the Qwen fit and placing the 235B MoE beyond the fit range are SFT and not orders-of-magnitude pretraining extrapolation.
All of it: no compute-optimal allocation is measured.
All of it: shape is not varied at a fixed parameter count.
Image, video and other modalities; transfer; a fitted power law in data volume (only three points).
Benchmarks across pretraining runs; loss-to-downstream relations across model sizes after fine-tuning.
Training-schedule and data effects on the original pretraining laws' exponents and compute-optimal split.

missing.what: MoE placement residuals against the dense size fit (geometric mean 0.016–0.022 vs active/total 0.021–0.073 nats; 235B lies beyond the fit range). This is parameter-counting dependence.
Validation NLL rises after about 2 epochs while the judged task score holds or rises through 8 epochs (loss–downstream divergence).
Base-model eval scores rise near-monotonically with size within each family on all four tasks.
Best SFT NLL falls monotonically with size on every dataset, and the Qwen and Llama families interleave.

record.verdict_notes: The data are generated to pass the same judge used downstream, so the V6 correlations are not independent. Exponent CIs are wide at six points. Fresh-example results confound examples with tokens. R21 double-counts R16–R19.

versions.untested_parts: The measured losses are from supervised fine-tuning, not held-out pretraining loss; the study does not test parameter-, token-, or compute-scaling when the other pretraining variables are not bottlenecks.

No small-run pretraining fit is used to predict much larger pretraining runs. Llama models are scored against a Qwen3 SFT size fit, and some MoE placements extrapolate the SFT fit, but neither is the claimed pretraining extrapolation test.
No fixed-compute comparison or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is measured.
The study compares model families and MoE placements, but does not hold parameter count fixed while varying depth, width, or architecture details to measure their effect on loss.
Tests supervised fine-tuning on text and fresh-example/repeated-pass settings; does not test image or video models, other modalities, or transfer as a scaling law.
Tests validation/test loss against customer-task evaluations within selected SFT settings, not broad downstream-task scaling across pretraining runs or benchmarks.

Shows SFT fit and data-setting dependence, including a refit under oracle learning rates; does not test how the original pretraining laws depend on parameter counting, pretraining schedules, or their fitting methods.

rows.subject: Nine base models
rows.size_stated: 1B–32B; nine models across Qwen3 and Llama families
